*o o, sixteenth (later fifteenth) letter in Gr. alphabet : as numeral o/ =
70 , but <*>o =
70 , 000 . The name of the letter was ou)=,
Pl. Cra. 414c , al., Callias ap. Ath. 10.453d , Neoptol. ap. eund. 10.454f , AP 9.385 ( Steph. Gramm.) : this name was in Plato's time pronounced like the letter itself, Pl. Cra. 393d ; o scanned long, Achae. 33.4 ; to\ o_ (v.l. ou<*>)
stoixei=on
Suid.
s.v. *filoce/nou gramma/tion ; later called o)\ mikro/n ( Hdn. Epim. 209 , Theognost. Can. 13 ),
little or
short o, opp. w)\ me/ga
great or
long o.

o(, h(, to/, is, when thus written, demonstr. Pronoun. in Att. , definite or prepositive Article. in Ep. , the so-called postpositive Article, = relative Pronoun, o(/s, h(/, o(/.—The nom. masc. and fem. sg. and pl., o(, h(, oi(, ai(, have no accent in codd. and most printed books, exc. when used as the relative ; but o(, h(, oi( , ai( differ only in writing from o(\, h(\, oi(\, ai(\ ; the nom. forms of the article are said by Hdn.Gr. 1.474 to be oxytone, and by A.D. Pron. 8.7 not to be enclitic. The forms tw=n, toi=s, tai=s were barytone (i. e. tw\n, toi\s, tai\s) in Aeol. acc. to Aristarch. ap. A.D. Synt. 51.26 . For oi( , ai( some dialects (not Cypr. , cf. Inscr.Cypr. 135.30H. , nor Cret., cf. Leg.Gort. 5.28 , nor Lesbian, cf. Alc. 81 , Sapph. Supp. 5.1 ) and Hom. have toi/, tai/ (though oi( , ai( are also found in Hom. ) : other Homeric forms
are gen. sg. toi=o, gen. and dat. dual toi=in
Od. 18.34
, al. : gen. pl. fem. ta/wn [a_], dat. toi=si, th=|s and th=|si, never tai=si or tai=s in Hom. — In Dor. and all other dialects exc. Att. and Ion. the fem. forms preserve the old a_ instead of changing it to h, hence Dor. etc. a(, ta/n, ta=s ; the gen. pl. ta/wn contracts in many dialects to ta=n ; the gen. sg. is in many places tw=, acc. pl. tw/s, but Cret., etc., to/ns ( Leg.Gort. 7.7 , al.) or to/s (ib. 3.50 , al.) ; in Lesbian Aeol. the acc. pl. forms are toi\s, tai\s,

ou)qei/s, ou)qe/n, later form for ou)dei/s, ou)de/n, found in Att. Inscrr. from 378 B.C. onwards along with ou)dei/s, which it supersedes entirely from about 325 B.C. to 100 B.C. (forty examples of q, none of d); ou)qei/s is in a majority in Ptolemaic papyri up to about 130 B.C., after which ou)dei/s begins to be common, but does not prevail until i A. D.; the evidence of non- Att. Inscrr. is in general agreement with the foregoing; codd. of Th. , Antipho , And. , Lys. , and Hdt. never have ou)qei/s, but the q forms are freq. in those of Pl. , X. , Isoc. , D. , Hyp. , Arist. , and Thphr. , freq. as variants for the d forms; also in Hellenistic writers, Teles , Plb. , etc.; the frequency of q forms in the uncials of LXX varies roughly according to the date (known or probable) of the translation of the book in question (though the d forms are in a large majority in the LXX as a whole); the q forms are rare in codd. of Str. and later writers.
